changed_by.title: feat: Tell the owner when the repository becomes public

changed_steps.step: Tell the owner what the public repository shows

lesson.summary: Nothing needs doing for #568: its first flag-public run filed #656 to tell the owner the repository is public. In the same run, close-duplicate.sh could not find #656 in the list of open tickets it had just been added to, so the check for a second copy filed at the same moment did not happen.
lesson.detail: Pull request #568 made flag-public.sh file one needs-human ticket when the repository becomes public. On its first run, "Tell the owner what the public repository shows" found no open ticket with that title. It filed #656, printed "told the owner that the repository is public: …/issues/656" and succeeded, so the change did what it claimed. A later change, not #568, added a call to close-duplicate.sh (decisions T620). That script lists open tickets newest first, and on this run the list did not hold #656 seconds after it was filed: jq stopped with "the list does not hold the ticket". The ticket stayed open, as flag-public.sh intends when that step fails. This run had no second copy, so nothing was lost. The same delay can make the duplicate step fail every time it runs, in flag-public.sh, cut-rule-files.sh and revert.sh. That belongs to open ticket #620, "Stop two runs filing the same ticket at once", not to this pull request.

cost.amount: Nothing: the run cost $0 and 0 turns, and it filed the one ticket it was meant to.

lesson.saves: Nothing: the change of #568 worked, and this run filed no second copy of the ticket.
